original_value: One of the most challenging problems in precision agriculture is to correctly identify and separate crops from the soil. Current precision farming algorithms based on artificially intelligent networks use multi-spectral or hyper-spectral data to derive radiometric indices that guide the operational management of agricultural complexes. Deep learning applications using these big data require sensitive filtering of raw data to effectively drive their hidden layer neural network architectures. Threshold techniques based on the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) or other similar metrics are generally used to simplify the development and training of deep learning neural networks. They have the advantage of being natural transformations of hyper-spectral or multi-spectral images that filter the data stream into a neural network, while reducing training requirements and increasing system classification performance. In this paper, to calculate a detailed crop/soil segmentation based on high resolution Digital Surface Model (DSM) data, we propose the redefinition of the radiometric index using a directional mathematical filter. To further refine the analysis, we feed this new radiometric index image of about 3500 × 4500 pixels into a relatively small Convolution Neural Network (CNN) designed for general image pattern recognition at 28 × 28 pixels to evaluate and resolve the vegetation correctly. We show that the result of applying a DSM filter to the NDVI radiometric index before feeding it into a Convolutional Neural Network can potentially improve crop separation hit rate by 65%.

result.paraphrase: Correctly distinguishing crops from soil is one of precision agriculture’s most difficult challenges. In current precision farming methods, AI-based networks rely on multi-spectral or hyper-spectral data to compute radiometric indices that support the management of agricultural systems. Deep learning systems built on these big data sets need careful filtering of raw data to effectively feed hidden-layer neural network architectures. Thresholding methods based on the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) or comparable metrics are commonly used to make deep learning neural networks easier to develop and train. These methods are useful because they naturally transform hyper-spectral or multi-spectral images, filtering the data stream into a neural network while lowering training demands and improving classification performance. In this paper, we propose redefining the radiometric index with a directional mathematical filter to compute detailed crop/soil segmentation from high-resolution Digital Surface Model (DSM) data. For further refinement, we input this new radiometric index image, approximately 3500 × 4500 pixels, into a relatively small Convolution Neural Network (CNN) intended for general image pattern recognition at 28 × 28 pixels in order to assess and correctly identify the vegetation. We demonstrate that applying a DSM filter to the NDVI radiometric index before sending it to a Convolutional Neural Network can potentially increase crop separation hit rate by 65%.
